title: fleet: add reservation-credit accounting + percentile utilization exporter
author: Aisha Thompson
description: Background and motivation: customers on Dedicated reported burst exhaustion when many small tenants concurrently requested capacity; existing burst token pool was working but visibility and credit reclamation were limited. This PR introduces a reservation-credit abstraction for fleets that lets controllers pre-authorize short-lived capacity (reservation credits), continuously decay unused credits, and expose percentile-based utilization metrics to drive smarter autoscaling decisions. The design goals are: 1) preserve latency SLOs for bursty tenants by allowing short pre-reservations without immediate allocation of GPU slots, 2) prevent long-lived starvation by decaying unused credits and reclaiming reservations, 3) give operators percentile-based utilization signals (p50/p95/p99) per-fleet and per-tenant to tune autoscaler policies, and 4) be backward compatible with existing token-bucket style burst pools. What changed (high level): implemented a reservation credit ledger persisted in etcd with sharded keys per-fleet; added a credit decayer that runs as a leader-elected controller to age and reclaim credits; extended the scheduler admission path to consult reservation credits before blocking or spinning up capacity; added a new Prometheus exporter and histograms to emit utilization percentiles and reservation latency distributions; exposed new config knobs for reservation window, decay half-life, and max-reservation-per-tenant. Backwards compatibility and migration: the migration copies current burst-token counts into the new ledger on upgrade; token-based allocations are still accepted but will be migrated to credits over a short window. Migration is guarded behind a feature-flag (env REDWOOD_ENABLE_RESERVATION_CREDITS) which defaults to off for initial rollout. Testing and validation: added unit tests for ledger accounting and decay math, integration tests that simulate concurrent reservations and reclamation, and a canary job that verifies metric emission under load. Benchmarks: on a synthetic mix of 80% small bursts and 20% long-running flows, tail latency regressions were eliminated and the average transient capacity churn decreased by ~18% compared to baseline. Risks and mitigations: new controller introduces leader election complexity and extra etcd load; mitigations include sharding keys and rate-limiting reconciliation loops. Rollout plan: enable behind feature flag, deploy controller to canary region, monitor new metrics (redwood_fleet_reservation_credit_total, redwood_fleet_reservation_util_p95) and errors, then flip the flag cluster-wide. Related work: builds on earlier burst-token work (see ENG-1862) but diverges by introducing time-decay accounting and percentile observability. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] telemetry dashboards - [x] migration path and feature flag - [x] docs update (operators guide)

review_comments: Diego Marquez (2026-02-16): Can you clarify the decay math and whether half-life is configurable? Also we should instrument the etcd request rate per shard so we can cap it if operators are on small clusters.

Aisha Thompson (2026-02-16): Decay uses exponential half-life; made half-life configurable via reservation.decay_half_life_seconds. Added a per-shard rate limiter and exposed etcd ops metrics in telemetry.
Rina Patel (2026-02-17): Scheduler change looks correct but we need a safety fallback if the ledger is unavailable at admission path (don't block traffic). Add a bypass path and strong logs.

Aisha Thompson (2026-02-17): Added admission fallback: if ledger probe fails, admission falls back to legacy token allocation and logs a metric redwood_fleet_reservation_ledger_probe_fail_total. Included tests to simulate etcd outage.
Oliver Zhang (2026-02-19): CI flaked in integration on the canary job; re-ran and added tighter timeouts to the canary harness. Approving once CI is green.
merge_outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-21 after green CI. Commit message condensed to: fleet: reservation credits ledger + decayer + telemetry. Backported small config to release/0.60 for hotfix safety
release_notes: Introduce reservation credits for fleet burst handling; emits new metrics: redwood_fleet_reservation_credit_total, redwood_fleet_reservation_util_p50/p95/p99, and redwood_fleet_reservation_latency_ms. Feature gated behind REDWOOD_ENABLE_RESERVATION_CREDITS. Operators should review docs/operators/reservation-credits.md before enabling.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in canary region, monitor new metrics for reservation saturation and ledger probe failures, use provided helm values to tune shard count and decay half-life. Migration script scripts/migrate_burst_to_credits.sh should be run during a low-traffic window.
